title: introduce-typesafe-rag-toolchain-quickstart-with-local-eval
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Add new Typesafe RAG quickstart demonstrating a minimal toolchain (TS + Python adapters), local eval harness, and devcontainer for reproducible developer flows. No breaking changes.
body:
Summary: Add a new quickstart that demonstrates a typesafe RAG toolchain focused on local developer ergonomics and reproducible regression testing. This quickstart provides a tiny TypeScript orchestrator, strongly typed tool interfaces, a Python retrieval adapter, a local eval harness with labeled prompt tests, and a devcontainer-based developer environment.

Motivation and context: Teams frequently iterate on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) stacks but lack a compact, typesafe example that ties together tool-calling, retrieval adapters, and local evaluation. Our existing quickstarts show RAG patterns but do not emphasize TypeScript typing for tool contracts or an on-ramp for writing prompt-level regression tests. This PR creates a minimal reference that product/eng teams can fork and use as a template for safe tool upgrades, prompt tests, and pre-merge quality gates. Linked Linear: ENG-8521 (RAG quickstart backlog), ENG-8799 (local eval harness).

What changed (high level):
- Add quickstart directory: quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/ with runnable example and README.
- TypeScript orchestrator (src/orchestrator.ts) that defines interfaces for tools (IToolInput, IToolOutput) and composes calls with strict typings.
- Python retrieval adapter (adapters/py_vector_adapter.py) that demonstrates how to wire a small FAISS-like vector store shim to the orchestrator via a lightweight HTTP adapter.
- Local eval harness (tools/local_eval/) with a small set of prompt/expected-output pairs and a runner script that produces a JSON results summary for CI.
- Devcontainer and docker-compose for reproducible local development (devcontainer.json, docker-compose.yml).
- CI job: quickstarts-typesafe-eval that runs the local eval harness on push to feature branches.

Files changed (representative):
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/README.md (new) -- explains intent, architecture, and usage.
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/src/orchestrator.ts (new) -- typed orchestrator and tool contracts.
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/src/tools/simple_qa_tool.ts (new) -- example tool implementing the contract.
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/adapters/py_vector_adapter.py (new) -- tiny Flask app exposing /search.
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/tools/local_eval/run_eval.sh (new) -- runs evals and emits results.json.
- quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain/devcontainer.json (new) + docker-compose.yml (new).
- .github/workflows/quickstarts-typesafe-eval.yml (new) -- CI job using the eval harness.

Commits (summary):
- add typesafe rag quickstart skeleton (initial files, README, licenses)
- implement ts orchestrator and example tool with types and unit tests
- add python retrieval adapter prototype and integration notes
- add local eval harness and CI workflow
- fix: CI runner path and permission for run_eval.sh

How to use locally (quickstart):
1) Clone repo and cd into quickstarts/typesafe-rag-toolchain.
2) Start the Python adapter: (cd adapters && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && FLASK_ENV=development python py_vector_adapter.py)
3) Open a new shell, install node deps (cd src && npm ci) and run the orchestrator with the provided .env pointing at the adapter.
4) Run ./tools/local_eval/run_eval.sh to execute the small suite of prompt/expected pairs. A results.json is produced containing pass/fail and token counts used for quick regression checks.

Testing and CI: The new workflow quickstarts-typesafe-eval runs on pushes to feature/* and PRs. Steps: checkout, start adapter under Docker, install node, run orchestrator in a headless mode against sample prompts, run local_eval runner, upload results as an artifact. The workflow currently marks required status checks for merging and will gate merges when the eval harness reports regressions. CI passed on this branch except for a transient lint warning that was addressed in the latest commit.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Owen Martinez (reviewer): "Nice compact example — can you add a short explanation in the README about why we chose typed tool contracts vs duck-typing?"
  - Author (Leah): "Added a paragraph in README + example interface comments explaining safety and catchable compile-time errors. Kept tradeoffs section short."
- Priya Raman (reviewer): "The eval harness is useful but the expected outputs are strict; do we want fuzzy scoring later?"
  - Leah: "Agreed — added TODO note and a small utility that computes token overlap. Follow-up task created (ENG-8987)."
- Marco Silva (reviewer): "Can the Python adapter be swapped with a hosted vector DB? Add instructions?"
  - Leah: "Yes — README includes a section 'Using a real vector service' with env var samples for running against a hosted endpoint."

Security and privacy notes: The Python adapter is intentionally minimal and not production hardened. README warns users that the example vector store is ephemeral and meant only for local dev. No secrets are checked in; the devcontainer uses env file templates.

Backward compatibility and breakage: This is an additive quickstart in the examples surface area. No runtime or API changes to the main platform. Marked breaking_change: false.

Follow-ups and related work:
- ENG-8987: add fuzzy scoring and semantic similarity thresholds to the eval harness.
- ENG-9042: add a Go adapter example requested by a community contributor (future).

Merge details: Squash merged to main on 2026-02-19 after approvals from reviewers. CI green at merge time.

Notes for maintainers: Keep the eval harness intentionally small (<= 10 canonical prompts) to prevent flaky CI and to lower maintenance burden. The types in src/orchestrator.ts are exported to make it easy for SDK authors to reference the same contracts when building tool scaffolding.

If you want to run the quickstart in CI yourself: see .github/workflows/quickstarts-typesafe-eval.yml and the README for env variables and expected artifacts.

End.
